pages.title: Contract Layer and RPC Protocol
pages.purpose: The src/contract package: MessagePort wire protocol (request/response/subscribe/unsubscribe/event), the Api method table, Streams topics, desktop bridge and browser/process type contracts, and the contract-coverage checker that keeps server handlers and client calls in sync.
instructions: Document how adding an Api method requires handler registration plus contract coverage.
Explain RpcServer/RpcClient mechanics and error encoding (RpcError, ToolchainError).
Note docs/rpc-protocol.md is referenced but absent; do not cite it.

pages.title: Process Architecture and Startup Flow
pages.purpose: The Electron process model (main, Agent Host utilityProcess, plugin/managed-process workers, renderer), boot sequence, ownership boundaries, and how MessagePort RPC plus parentPort supervision wire the processes together.
instructions: Cite src/main/main.ts header comment and host-manager.ts for ownership claims.
Cover host supervision: ready/ping-pong heartbeat, restart budget, status fan-out to renderer.
Describe the three-process split and which side owns window chrome vs agent business logic.

pages.title: Change Guides
pages.purpose: Focused recipes for representative maintenance tasks with the exact files and checks to touch: adding an RPC/Api method, adding a toolchain capability or catalog component, adding a renderer setting with i18n, adding a channel adapter, and extending managed-process policy — each with verification commands.
instructions: Derive every step from real code structure; do not invent scaffolding that does not exist.
Each recipe: goal, files, invariants to preserve, focused validation command(s).
Link to the owning system page for background rather than repeating it.

pages.title: Testing and Verification Pipeline
pages.purpose: How to validate changes: node:test *.test.mjs suites and custom runner, per-domain integration scripts (managed-process workflows/flood/frameworks, browser Electron + agent E2E, tsup watch, NSIS upgrade), smoke harness against built output, and the verify.mjs gate ordering that blocks packaging.
instructions: Explain how to run one focused test file and the timeout knob PI_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS.
Map verify steps to commands so contributors can run the gate locally.
Note test isolation requirement enforced by smoke-electron-isolation test.

pages.title: Build, Packaging, and Release
pages.purpose: How the app is built and shipped: tsup entry matrix (main CJS, Host/workers ESM, preload), Vite renderer build, dev orchestration, electron-builder config and extra resources, bundled tool preparation, Windows helper build/SBOM/reproducibility checks, macOS signing/notarization scripts, production artifact checks, and the CI matrix in build-desktop.yml.
instructions: Explain the PI_DESKTOP_EXPECTED_PI_VERSION define and packaged startup validation flag.
Map each CI job stage to the local equivalent command.
Note packaged-cleanup-fault validation entry in main.ts.

pages.title: Electron Main Shell and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Main-process desktop concerns: window creation and navigation policy, single instance, deep links (pi-agent-desktop://), tray/badge, app:// protocol and CSP, UI-state persistence, logging, diagnostics export with redaction, renderer crash recovery, host-restart recovery, quit cleanup ordering, and auto-update state machine.
instructions: Cite specific line ranges for heartbeat/restart budget constants.
Cover updater gating: platform support, packaged/test mode, install prepare/recover hooks.
Order the shutdown path: before-quit dialog, managed-process cleanup, browser dispose, host stop.

pages.title: Security Model and Hardening
pages.purpose: Cross-cutting security invariants: sandboxed renderer with contextIsolation, IPC sender trust checks, app:// CSP, navigation/window policies, credential vaults (safeStorage channels secrets, browser secret vault), managed-process containment, toolchain download integrity (checksums, secure extraction), diagnostics/log redaction, and the automated desktop-security invariant checker.
instructions: Cover what each redaction layer strips.
Note sandbox/permission configuration in window.ts and menu-policy.ts.
Prefer invariant checks and policies that tests enforce over general advice.

pages.title: Agent Host: Sessions and Runtime
pages.purpose: The Agent Host process internals: RPC handler registration, pi-coding-agent session lifecycle in rpc-manager, session persistence/index/history/watcher, titles and compaction, toolchain-aware bash/search/git tools, and parent-rpc back-calls into main.
instructions: Cover extension surfaces: skills, plugins via worker thread, model/auth runtime.
Distinguish Host-owned logic from main-process delegation via parent-rpc.
Explain where session transcripts persist (pi agent dir via SessionManager/getAgentDir) and how the index caches by file fingerprint.

pages.title: Embedded Browser Subsystem
pages.purpose: User/Agent shared browser: main-process BrowserService, profiles and tab restore, CDP coordinator, network policy/interception, permission grants and authorization coordinators, secret vault and redaction, downloads, header rules, and how capability snapshots drive Host-side browser tools.
instructions: Cover confirmation flows (user consent, agent authorization, persistent grants).
Note certificate-error and proxy-credential hooks wired in main.ts.
Separate main-process browser runtime from Host tool surface and the browser:init/changed ack loop.

pages.title: Messaging Channels (WeChat, Telegram, Feishu)
pages.purpose: External chat channels: adapter registry and per-channel adapters, inbound policy/pairing, session bindings and lane scheduler, media store, config/state stores with atomic 0600 writes, secret access via main credential vault, redaction, and outbound rendering.
instructions: Cover where secrets live (main CredentialVault, channels.secrets.json) vs config/state files.
Note pairing TTL and rate/limit constants with sources.
Trace one inbound message from adapter to Pi session turn and back outbound.

pages.title: Managed Background Processes
pages.purpose: Dev-server/watcher containment: Host managed-process service and backends (POSIX process groups, Windows Job helper), output buffering/cursors, policies and rate limits, main-side reaper journal, owner identity generation, LAN-bind confirmation, shutdown cleanup deadline, and tray counts.
instructions: Cover the native Windows helper's role and its build/reproducibility checks.
Explain why cleanup is a hard gate before Host restart and app quit.
Note capability projection gates the feature per platform/reaper/owner state.

pages.title: Renderer UI and Preload Bridge
pages.purpose: React renderer architecture: App shell and components, hooks (useAgentSession, active-session live sync), api/agent clients over the transferred MessagePort, event-stream connection policy, drafts/layout preferences, i18n and theming, plus the preload piBridge contract and early-event replay.
instructions: Cover renderer state sync: subscribe streams, pagination, unread tracking.
Explain MessagePort transfer via window.postMessage and why contextBridge cannot carry ports.
Note i18n checker scripts enforce dictionary invariants.

pages.title: Developer Toolchain Management
pages.purpose: Cross-platform tool provisioning: runtime catalog schema, discovery/probes, downloader and secure extractor, managed component installer, bundled core (rg/fd), custom tool registration, project detection, per-project resolution, and how snapshots are acked into the Host and applied to agent tool environments.
instructions: Cite the focus-rescan TTL and intent/trusted validation in main.ts request handler.
Cover environment sanitization and Windows portable-git path handling.
Trace snapshot propagation: main ToolchainManager -> HostManager toolchain:init/changed -> Host ack revision.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: environment requirements, install, dev/build/test/verify commands, packaged startup validation, where to look first for common maintenance tasks.
instructions: Ground every command in package.json scripts or the referenced script source.
Route readers to the narrowest system page for deeper work; do not duplicate system explanations.
Show the shortest working loop: npm ci, npm run dev, npm test, npm run verify.
